Definition: from G2784; a herald, i.e. of divine truth (especially of the gospel):--preacher.
BiblicalUsage: Keryx means a herald, a preacher of divine truth. 1 Timothy 2:7 says, whereunto I am ordained a preacher, and an apostle, a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and verity. 2 Timothy 1:11 says the same, I am appointed a preacher, and an apostle, and a teacher. 2 Peter 2:5 says God saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the herald is appointed, not self-made: Paul was ordained and appointed, and Noah preached righteousness while the world drowned. I hold that the preacher's job is the same in every age, to speak the truth in Christ and not lie.
